fields.outcome: A documentation author can render a generic AutoTour journey as independently replaceable module videos suitable for review and CI artifacts.
fields.scope: Record one deterministic Playwright WebM per journey module while preserving browser-context state between modules. Store stable asset references in the walkthrough manifest and expose a library API. Exclude MP4 transcoding, Remotion composition, audio, DOM replay, and publication hosting.
fields.acceptance: Executing a multi-module fixture journey with video enabled produces a playable non-empty WebM for every module and records deterministic module asset paths without exposing secrets.
fields.decisions: Use one browser context and a separate page per module. Playwright finalizes each module video when its page closes; stable output names are applied afterward. Video is generated media and remains ignored by Git by default.
fields.verification: Run the video capture against the local fixture in Chromium, assert one non-empty WebM per module, validate manifest asset references, and run package and frozen AgentHouse checks.
fields.changes: Implemented in commit 25d1306: one Playwright WebM per module using separate pages in a shared browser context, deterministic module asset paths, environment-backed input masking, headless fixed-viewport capture, CI Chromium installation, and a live AgentHouse DealDesk example journey.
fields.dependencies: Consumes the generic executor from st-04 and Playwright video recording. CI publishing is a later story.
fields.risks: Video encoding depends on browser availability, page closure is required to finalize files, and animations or remote content can make output nondeterministic.

criteria.expectation: Each executed module produces its own non-empty WebM file.
Authentication and browser-context state carry from one module recording to the next.
Video files and manifest references use deterministic module-based paths.
Pages and browser context close on success or failure and finalized videos are not reported before they exist.
Video metadata, paths, returned values, and diagnostics contain no credential values.
Video capture runs headlessly with fixed viewport and generated files stay in ignored output paths.
